triggerReason: Causal traces exposed agent decisions, but policy logic, cooldowns, and arbitration were still embedded in the simulation step.
action: Introduced a formal agent runtime with independent policies, capability contracts, per-agent and global budgets, cooldowns, priorities, risk ceilings, conflict resolution, and ARIA coordination.
outcome: Agents now compete and cooperate through proposals instead of mutating the world, while every scheduling or rejection decision remains observable.
evidence: 500-tick conformance test keeps every command within capability and budget contracts
All four domain agents receive scheduled work without starvation
Cooldown, per-agent budget, global budget, risk ceiling, and metric conflicts are tested
ARIA explains the latest scheduling decision and can pause or resume the run
Rejected proposals receive complete trace and evaluation records
